text:
sophie-support: Escalation from ACME (tenant acme-123). Since 03:12 UTC their traffic to Dedicated pool 'acme-gold' started getting 429s and elevated latency. Customer reports service degraded after an autoscale event. They see many requests landing in 'shared-burst' pool instead of their reserved pool. Can we triage?

mike-eng: Do we have a sample request id + headers? If requests are being routed to shared pool that suggests a routing policy mismatch or header parsing bug.

sophie-support: Sample from customer (sanitized):

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' \  -H 'x-tenant-id: acme-123' \n  -H 'x-redwood-tier: gold, premium' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4x","input":"hi"}'

Response headers:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
routing-pool: shared-burst

sophie-support: Customer says before autoscale everything was fine — they have a Reserved Dedicated pool with capacity. After we scaled up the pool, a subset of their requests began going to shared pool and getting throttled. They observed a spike coincident with a control-plane deploy at 03:10 UTC.

julia-infra: I see related logs in control-plane at 03:10:05 UTC: 
"WARN parseTierHeader: header=\"gold, premium\" parsed=[\"gold\"] -> fallbackPool=shared-burst"

alan-oncall: That log looks suspicious. Why did the parser drop the second token and pick default fallback pool? We should check the CSV splitting logic — there was a small change last week to 'trim and dedupe' header tokens. Maybe it mishandles spaces after comma.

infra-sre: Reproducer I ran locally: when header is exactly 'gold,premium' we route correctly to acme-gold. When header is 'gold, premium' (note the space) the parser returns only 'gold' but then matches an older routing rule that falls through to shared. Minimal repro (curl):

curl -H "x-tenant-id: acme-123" -H "x-redwood-tier: gold, premium" https://routing.debug.internal/route?req=r-0a1b2c3d
# response:
# {"route":"shared-burst","match":"tier-header-parse-fallthrough"}

mike-eng: Confirmed. The CSV split in the control-plane code used String.split(',') but then compared tokens to policy keys without trimming; we recently added a normalization change that treats tokens with trailing spaces as distinct and then fails to match exact 'gold'+'premium' composite rule. That makes the policy evaluator take the next fallback (shared).

julia-infra: Impact: any tenant sending comma+space list in tier header could get misrouted. ACME's SDK emits 'gold, premium' (with space) from our client library variant. Ouch.

alan-oncall: Mitigation: hotfix the parser to trim tokens and normalize (lowercase) before policy matching. Also add a temporary rule: prefer dedicated pools if tenant has reservation key ignoring small token mismatch. Can we deploy a hotfix to control-plane?

devops-bot: deploy/control-plane-parser-fix started by julia-infra at 03:45 UTC · sha: ab12cd3 · canary 10%

infra-sre: Patch submitted:
```
- tokens = header.split(',')
+ tokens = header.split(',').map(t => t.trim().toLowerCase())
```
Will add unit tests for 'gold, premium' and 'gold,premium' cases.

mike-eng: Also add acceptance test that uses our SDK variants (node/python/go) because different SDKs format headers differently.

lina-account: ACME is on a client call now. They're very upset — asked for immediate credit for throttled requests. What's the ask?

sophie-support: We proactively offered 72 hours of credits and a postmortem; customer accepted the credits but wants ETA on fix and confirmation their traffic won't be throttled further.

alan-oncall: Current ETA: canary patch underway, will evaluate metrics for 15m then roll to 100% if stable. If anything goes wrong we will revert.

devops-bot: canary at 10% Healthy. latencies normal.

infra-sre: After canary rollout observed routing-pool flip for sample traffic -> now returns 'acme-gold' for header 'gold, premium'. Verified for both SDK header formats.

mike-eng: I'll follow up with a git PR to add stricter parsing tests and update changelog. Postmortem draft should include: root cause (parser trimming regression), timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps (hotfix + fallback policy), and long-term fix (policy matcher tolerant to whitespace).

sophie-support: Noted. Action items: (1) finalize rollback/fix if canary fails (alan), (2) postmortem draft (mike), (3) confirm credits applied (lina), (4) add SDK header tests (julia).

lina-account: Confirmed credits applied to acme-123 billing account. I'll notify customer and share ETA.

alan-oncall: Closing loop: 100% rollout completed at 03:59 UTC, no regressions observed. Marking resolved for now; will follow up with postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

sophie-support: Thanks all. Customer very appreciative of quick response.

mike-eng: Postmortem link to follow.
